issues.title: Obtain the county's 2026 appropriation ordinance
issues.detail: Found on clarkcountyar.gov and the state transparency portal. Ingested; it is the money trail tree.

stamped.revealed: The county appropriates $21,386,230 across roughly 40 funds for 2026. Public safety (sheriff, jail, 911) is about 43% of the General Fund. The tree above is this ordinance, made navigable.

issues.title: City of Arkadelphia budget
issues.detail: The budget document itself is not posted online; obtaining it is a city hall counter visit and the city manager conversation.

stamped.revealed: The city's audited financials ARE online even though its budget is not. FY2022, FY2023, and FY2024 city audits plus the FY2023 water & sewer system audit are now stored in the document library. FY2024 (regulatory basis): general fund revenues $18.2M, expenditures $13.2M, year-end balance $2.3M.

research_notes: What the internet answers: audited actuals (layer two) for the city, 2022–2024, via Arkansas Legislative Audit.
What it cannot answer: the budget document itself — line items, department detail, city salaries. That remains a records request at city hall.

issues.title: School district budgets & millage breakdown
issues.detail: Arkadelphia Public Schools + Gurdon. District offices and state education records.

stamped.revealed: School millage — the largest line on most residents' tax bills — is now sourced: Arkadelphia 47.65 mills (25.0 M&O + 2.0 other M&O + 17.65 bond + 3.0 other bond), Gurdon 43.0. Both districts' FY2024 audits are stored. The Arkadelphia district has pledged property taxes against $35.05M in bonds issued 2021–2022. And the 2025 millage book shows Arkadelphia 3.0 mills higher than the 2024 book — new bond mills.

research_notes: What the internet answers: audited district financials (Arkansas Legislative Audit), millage with full M&O/bond breakdown (DESE + state millage books), statewide comparison data (MySchoolInfo).

What it cannot answer yet: the districts' own budget documents with line-item detail. Arkadelphia posts state-required financial documents at arkadelphiaschools.org — worth a targeted pull as a follow-up.
Fringe complication mapped: parts of Clark County are in Bismarck, Centerpoint, Delight, and Harmony Grove districts — tax bills differ by where in the county you live.

issues.title: Millage rate sheet & sales tax inventory
issues.detail: The revenue side of the whole tree: every mill, every dedicated sales tax, what each costs a $100,000 home.

stamped.revealed: The millage half is answered from the state's own millage books (2024 and 2025 editions stored). County 7.1 mills — including road 3.0, library 1.0, hospital 1.0, and college 1.0 — plus city mills (Arkadelphia 5.0, Gurdon 5.4) and school mills (43.0–47.65). Total in Arkadelphia city limits: 59.75 mills ≈ $1,195/year on a $100,000 home before the homestead credit.

research_notes: Still open — the sales tax half: rates, sunset dates, and enacting ordinances for the EDCCC and fire sales taxes. The ordinances live in the county's online ordinance archive (see Docket #9's portal).

Urgency note: local reporting (July 2026) says the county owes the state ~$1.3M in sales-tax rebate repayments. News lead, not yet a corpus document — the underlying paperwork is exactly what this docket item exists to ingest.
Small ambiguity, labeled on the millage line: the exact mapping of the county's general/misc mills between city and rural residents needs a visual check of the millage book's table layout.

issues.title: The complete fire funding map
issues.detail: District budgets + dues + millage + city FD + the county's $45,921 pass-through. Prerequisite for framing the fire chief's founding question honestly.

stamped.revealed: The structure is mapped: Clark County levies no fire millage (confirmed in the state millage book), so rural departments run on dues, donations, and the county's $45,921 pass-through, while the Arkadelphia FD is funded inside the city budget (whose audits are now stored). Departments identified: Arkadelphia FD, East Clark County Rural VFD, Okolona VFD, Whelen Springs VFD, and the Clark County Fire Association (501(c)(3), postcard filer — no public financials).

research_notes: What the internet answers: the funding architecture, the department roster, and the fact that no fire millage exists here.
What it cannot answer: each department's dues schedule, membership counts, and finances — postcard 990s publish nothing. That detail is the fire chief conversation and counter visits.
The honest-framing caveat from the corpus stands: the county's $45,921 is a slice, not the whole picture.

issues.title: EDCCC incentives — who receives the $1.84M?
issues.detail: Recipient list, agreements, performance terms. EDCCC records and quorum court minutes; FOIA if needed.

stamped.revealed: The internet cannot name the recipients — and now we know why: EDCCC does not appear in the IRS exempt-organization file at all, so there are no public 990s to read. It is administered through the Arkadelphia Alliance (whose separate 501(c)(6) files 990s showing ~$800K/year of its own revenue). The recipient trail runs through EDCCC board minutes and quorum court minutes — offline or in the county's document portal.

research_notes: Entity map: EDCCC (owns the 991-acre Southwest Arkansas Mega Site; 15-member board; CEO Shelley Short) · Arkadelphia Regional Economic Development Alliance, 501(c)(6), EIN 26-2859118 (administers; 990s on ProPublica) · Clark County Industrial Council, 501(c)(6), EIN 58-1763488 (postcard filer).

The tax is a voter-approved half-cent county sales tax. Fund 3407 appropriations across stored budgets: $1,960,273 (2022) → $1,872,787 (2025) → $1,844,538 (2026) — drifting down, consistent with the rebate-clawback pressure on sales tax receipts.

Governance now documented in the OCR'd minutes: the county judge nominates and the quorum court approves EDCCC board members (Goodman & King, Dec 2024 11-0; Taylor, Franklin & Seale, 2026 9-0); CEO Short delivers quarterly reports to the court. Board roster (from the Alliance site): chair Lori Ross (Citizens Bank), vice chair Bill Conine, secretary Wilma Gill, treasurer Terry Bird (Bank of Delight), plus Franklin, Goodman, Griffin, Jester, King, Kirksey, Marlar, Orsburn, Seale, Shepherd, Taylor. Meets six times a year, noon, Fairfield Inn & Suites, Arkadelphia — public participation expanded June 2026 after data-center pushback.
First named spending recipient (news lead): Bailey Construction and Consulting, ~$1.95M Gum Springs site development approved March 2025, half covered by a $1M AEDC grant.

News leads from the Arkadelphian's EDCCC archive (leads, not corpus documents): July 2026 — county owes state ~$1.3M in sales-tax rebate repayments; April–May 2026 — 'Project Pulse' data-center land deal at Gum Springs terminated after the buyer missed its deposit; April 2026 — EDCCC selected for a state site-development grant (~$5.9M ask with 20% county match); February 2026 — bought 9 more acres at the Gurdon industrial site; June 2026 — board moving to increase public participation in meetings.

Next concrete step — likely the easiest big unlock: the minutes show CEO Short gives the quorum court quarterly reports with handouts and slides. Those materials became county records at the clerk's table; requesting the last 8 quarters is on the records-run list. Then the enacting ordinance from the county archive, and FOIA the incentive agreements if the reports don't name terms.

issues.title: Neighboring county salary schedules
issues.detail: Garland, Hot Spring, Nevada, Pike, Ouachita — same ordinance type, same public availability. The deputy-pay-parity comparison table.

stamped.revealed: The side-by-side table is live at /compare/deputy-pay, built from each county's own filed documents. Headline: Garland County's 2026 patrol deputies are listed at $57,418–$58,540 (65 positions) versus Clark's $43,398–$46,498 — and Garland's own 2024 survey showed ~$42,770, meaning they raised deputy pay roughly $15,000 in two years. Nevada pays $32,400 flat; Pike's 2024 figure was $43,202. Ouachita pools deputies into one line (not per-deputy comparable); Hot Spring's filings are scans awaiting OCR.

research_notes: Remaining: an OCR pass on the Hot Spring and Pike 2026 filings (stored as image-only scans), which would complete all five neighbors at 2026 rates.

New (2026-07-18): the county's own base-pay ordinances (2016–2025, all stored and OCR'd) show deputy starting pay rose 32% in four years — $32,898 in 2022 to $43,398 in 2026. The comparison page now carries the trajectory alongside the gap: the court has been raising pay steadily; Garland moved further, faster. Two deputy slots were pending applicants when Ordinance 2025-22 passed.

issues.title: Remaining line-item pages of the county ordinance
issues.detail: Sheriff, Jail, Assessor, District Court, Prosecutor, Juvenile, OEM, Coroner, Health, Circuit Judge, Extension, Veterans — plus the ~20 smaller special funds and page-level references for every number already ingested. The pages exist in the filed document; finish the ingestion.

stamped.revealed: The 96-page budget packet is stored and page-pinning has begun: 29 amounts now cite their exact page, applied only after an automated keyword check against the page text. 70 more amounts appear on multiple pages and await one-by-one review; the department line-item pages themselves are the next ingestion push.

issues.title: Legislative audit reports & treasurer's reports
issues.detail: arklegaudit.gov. Layer two of the money trail: what was actually spent vs. appropriated, findings, and fund restrictions on the ~$3.9M in unappropriated balances.

stamped.revealed: County audits for FY2021, FY2022, and FY2023 are stored (FY2024 not yet published by the state), and the findings sections are now published at /audits: the auditors reported no material weaknesses and no reportable noncompliance for the county (FY2023), the city (FY2022–24), the water system, or either school district — quoted and cited. Opacity documented elsewhere on this site is not misconduct; the referee's verdicts are clean.

research_notes: Treasurer's monthly/annual reports are not online — county records request.
FY2023 audit context found in the state's summary: the county's short-term financing debt limit was $8.65M at the end of 2023.

issues.title: Quorum court minutes & 2026 amendments
issues.detail: Ordinance amendments change this tree mid-year. Minutes feed outcome tracking.

stamped.revealed: Archived: all 38 quorum court minutes documents for 2024–2026 (regular sessions, budget committee, personnel committee, special sessions) pulled from the county's document portal into inbox/minutes/ — including the budget committee meetings that wrote the 2026 budget. They are scanned images without a text layer, so an OCR pass is queued before they can be searched and ingested.

research_notes: OCR complete (2026-07-18): 35 of 38 minutes now machine-readable after fixing a scan-decoding bug (1-bit images sheared by row padding; pipeline/lib-ocr.js corrects it). 3 files failed to download from the portal.

What the readable minutes document: the full 2025–26 ambulance saga (RFQs from Valor and Pafford → public comment with both owners speaking → Valor awarded → contract stalls in review → Valor closes, staff move to Pafford → county pivots to a Pafford contract), EDCCC quarterly reports delivered to the court by CEO Shelley Short, EDCCC board appointments made by the court, county property purchases, and every budget-season vote.

Equally important — what is NOT in the minutes: no asphalt, fuel, or gravel bid awards appear in any quorum court session. Commodity purchasing runs through the county judge's office, which means the check register FOIA (Docket #10) is the only path to those vendor names.
The quorum court meets the second Monday of each month — now in the platform's calendar config.

issues.title: County check register (layer three)
issues.detail: Which vendor got which check. Public under Arkansas FOIA; not posted. The floor beneath the floor.

stamped.revealed: The 'Who gets paid' page is live at /vendors with every payee a public document has named so far — Pioneer Civil Construction ($1.58M landfill closure), Total Assessment Solutions ($825,840 reappraisal), Southern Bancorp (county's lender), the 2021 road-bond holders ($8.46M principal, ~$1.08M interest through 2036, repaid by a pledged 0.5% sales tax), and the Valor→Pafford ambulance contract saga (news lead). The asphalt, fuel, and gravel suppliers remain unnamed in any posted document — and the page now carries a ready-to-send Arkansas FOIA request for the check register and bid tabulations.

research_notes: The audits also surfaced a reverse trail: gas and oil companies reimbursed the county's road fund $715,948 in 2023.
Sending the FOIA letter is a human step — any Arkansas citizen can; the template is on the /vendors page.
